solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cabinet door to be fixed: source latest info here (6,5)

indicators.note: something to be fixed is not yet in order, so the letters need rearranging

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: A handyman's job list notes a broken cabinet door and tells staff where to check for updates.
annotation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'to be fixed' look like a repair note, when it is the instruction to rearrange 'Cabinet door'.
annotation.definitionFit: A notice board is where the latest information is pinned up for people to read.

entries.clue: Drama from Norwegian of humble beginnings (3)

indicators.note: the beginnings of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of Norwegian, Of, Humble

annotation.surface: A play is said to come from a Norwegian of modest origins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of humble beginnings' reads as a biography of the playwright; 'beginnings' actually takes the first letter of each word, including 'Norwegian' itself. Noh is classical Japanese theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: Noh is a traditional form of Japanese drama.

entries.clue: Clan’s note welcoming supportive member (5)

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so the note holds the other piece

blocks.note: te, the seventh note of tonic sol-fa
a rib is a bone that supports the chest

annotation.surface: A clan sends a note of welcome to a helpful new member.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. 'Member' is a body part here, not a clan member.
annotation.definitionFit: A clan and a tribe are both groups of related families.

entries.clue: Horseman mounted donkey in turn to one side (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the word reads bottom to top
the reversed donkey goes inside the other word

blocks.note: to cock your head is to turn it to one side
ass = donkey, reversed to SSA and put inside CO…CK

annotation.surface: A horseman climbs onto a donkey and it veers off sideways.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' looks like riding, which suits the horseman; in a down clue it means reading upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: The Cossacks were famed as horsemen of the Russian and Ukrainian steppe.

entries.clue: Kylie having mare: bongo out of sync! (9)

indicators.note: letters out of sync are out of their proper order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Kylie is having a nightmare of a gig because the bongo player can't keep time.
annotation.walkthrough: Kylie looks like the singer Kylie Minogue, and 'having a mare' is British slang for going badly. In Australian English a kylie is a boomerang.
annotation.definitionFit: Kylie is a Western Australian Aboriginal word for a boomerang.

entries.clue: Running across a motorway south of Lincoln? (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so it comes after

blocks.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president
a as printed
M, as in the M1 or M25

annotation.surface: A road-atlas question: does a motorway run across the country south of the city of Lincoln?
annotation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city, which suits the motorway; it is the president. Abeam is a sailing term: at right angles to the ship's length.
annotation.definitionFit: Something abeam lies across a ship's line, at right angles to its keel.

entries.clue: Publisher of numerous titles retired, saddled with arrears (7)

indicators.note: to be saddled with something is to carry it, so the arrears hold the other piece

blocks.note: arrears = debt
ret. is the abbreviation for retired

annotation.surface: A prolific publisher has retired but is still stuck with unpaid bills.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Numerous titles' suggests many books; Debrett's publishes guides to the peerage, full of titled people.
annotation.definitionFit: Debrett's Peerage lists the titles of the British aristocracy.

entries.clue: Godsend in a climate crisis? Days no longer starting gloomy (3)

indicators.note: the word no longer has its starting letter

blocks.note: gloomy = dark
D is the abbreviation for days; it is the starting letter that gets dropped

annotation.surface: Someone in a climate crisis longs for a saviour, since the days are no longer dark and gloomy.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: in the Flood, the worst climate crisis on record, Noah's ark was the godsend.
annotation.definitionFit: Noah's ark saved its passengers from the Flood, a climate disaster if ever there was one.

entries.clue: Very unusual hole in one creature shot in Coleridge (9)

blocks.note: the golf score of three under par on one hole; on a par-four that means a single stroke
the seabird the Ancient Mariner kills with his crossbow in Coleridge's poem

annotation.surface: An odd pair of facts: a rare golf feat, and the animal killed in a famous poem.
annotation.walkthrough: An albatross is rarer than an ordinary hole in one because it needs one stroke on a par-four hole. 'Shot' links the two halves: a golf shot and a crossbow shot.
annotation.definitionFit: Both the golf score and the seabird of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner are called an albatross.

entries.clue: Finding idle amusement when slaughter occurs? (7,4)

definitions.text: Finding idle amusement when slaughter occurs?

blocks.note: the everyday reading: passing the hours idly while waiting
the literal reading: the hour at which the slaughter happens

annotation.surface: A dark joke about someone who amuses themselves idly while a massacre takes place.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is the ordinary meaning; the second takes the phrase literally, as the hour of the slaughter.
annotation.definitionFit: Killing time means occupying yourself idly while you wait.

entries.clue: Address: perhaps Mick Jagger dropped round (9)

blocks.note: to hail someone is to address them
Mick Jagger is a Rolling Stone

annotation.surface: An address book entry notes that Mick Jagger once popped by.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropped round' reads as visited; here it is a round thing that drops from the sky.
annotation.definitionFit: A hailstone is a round pellet of ice that falls from the clouds.

entries.clue: Stunning woman left making confused sound (5)

blocks.note: babe = attractive woman
L = left

annotation.surface: A beautiful woman leaves, and people mutter in bewilderment.
annotation.walkthrough: Babel, from the tower in Genesis, means a confused noise of many voices.
annotation.definitionFit: A babel is a confused noise of many voices, after the tower where languages were mixed up.

entries.clue: Salt brill — tons consumed (7)

blocks.note: brill (brilliant) and ace are both slang for excellent
T = tons
consumed = ate

annotation.surface: Salted brill, and tons of it eaten: a fishmonger's day.
annotation.walkthrough: Brill looks like the flatfish, and 'salt' like seasoning for it; brill is British slang for brilliant, and a salt is a chemical compound.
annotation.definitionFit: A chemistry sense: salts are named after their acid, and acetic acid (in vinegar) forms this one.

entries.clue: Outline a stupid speech where nothing’s deleted (11)

indicators.note: nothing is O, and it is taken out of the word

blocks.note: a as printed
dumb = stupid
an oration is a speech
O looks like zero; it is removed from ORATION, leaving RATION

annotation.surface: Someone sketches a foolish speech in which nothing gets cut.
annotation.walkthrough: A speech 'where nothing's deleted' sounds uncut; the nothing is the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: An adumbration is a sketchy outline or foreshadowing of something.

entries.clue: Artemis dances for eminent musicians (7)

indicators.note: letters that dance move about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: The goddess Artemis dances to music played by great performers.
annotation.walkthrough: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed Italian plural: maestro, 'master', is the honorific given to great conductors and performers.

entries.clue: Asian last character to remain in United Kingdom (5)

indicators.note: the pieces go inside United Kingdom

blocks.note: UK = United Kingdom
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
to be = to exist, to remain

annotation.surface: An Asian man, the last of his line, hopes to stay on in Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Last character' sounds like the final person; it is the last letter, Z.
annotation.definitionFit: An Uzbek is a person from Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

entries.clue: Starts to venture overseas in spare time: travel well (3,6)

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters
those letters go inside the phrase for spare time

blocks.note: spare = bony (lean), time = age; BONY AGE holds the letters
first letters of Venture and Overseas

annotation.surface: Advice to begin exploring abroad in your free time and enjoy the trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spare time' reads as leisure, but it splits: spare means bony, as in a spare, lean frame. The definition is a wish, as the phrase is.
annotation.definitionFit: Bon voyage is what you say to wish someone a good journey.

entries.clue: Influential jazzman has power blowing hard (9)

blocks.note: arm = power, as in the long arm of the law
a strong wind is one blowing hard

annotation.surface: A great jazz trumpeter plays with power, blowing his horn hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blowing hard' describes a trumpeter, which fits Louis Armstrong perfectly; in the wordplay it is a strong wind.
annotation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong was one of the most influential figures in jazz.

entries.clue: When drunk sing Moon River for Catholic dignitary (9)

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
R = river

annotation.surface: A tipsy clergyman bursts into the song Moon River.
annotation.walkthrough: Moon River is a well-known song, which makes 'River' look like part of a title rather than the letter R.
annotation.definitionFit: Monsignor is a title of honour for senior Catholic priests.

entries.clue: Popular movement to ostracise fwightful person? (9)

blocks.note: to ban someone is to shut them out
a frightful person is a dragon; 'fwightful' tells us to say it with W for R, as DWAGON

annotation.surface: A crowd turns on a frightening person, told in baby talk.
annotation.walkthrough: The misspelling 'fwightful' is the signal: the dragon must be pronounced the same way, as DWAGON.
annotation.definitionFit: A bandwagon is a popular cause or trend that people rush to join.

entries.clue: Enchanting twins come to disavow origins? (7)

indicators.note: to disavow the origins is to give up the first letters

blocks.note: TWINS without its first letter
COME without its first letter

annotation.surface: Charming twins arrive only to deny where they come from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Origins' reads as family background; it is the first letter of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: Winsome means charming or engaging.

entries.clue: The writer is taken aback about periodically harsh language (5)

indicators.note: taken back means the words are turned round
the reversed words go round the other piece
at regular intervals: every other letter

blocks.note: the writer = I, so 'the writer is' = I AM
the even letters of hArSh

annotation.surface: An author is shocked by the occasional coarse language someone uses.
annotation.walkthrough: I A M goes round AS to make IASAM, which read backwards is MASAI. 'Harsh language' looks like one phrase, but 'language' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Masai (Maa) is the language of the Masai people of Kenya and Tanzania.

entries.clue: Drink Bond likes can ruin one’s clothing (7)

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the outer letters wrap the can

blocks.note: to mar = to spoil or ruin
a tin is a can
I = one; MAR and I together clothe TIN

annotation.surface: Spilling James Bond's favourite cocktail can spoil your clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' and 'clothing' look like the risk to a smart suit; can is a tin and clothing wraps it.
annotation.definitionFit: James Bond famously orders a martini, shaken, not stirred.

entries.clue: Cherished houses close to Wimbledon decorated (7)

indicators.note: to house is to hold inside
the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: cherished = adored
last letter of Wimbledon

annotation.surface: Treasured homes near Wimbledon, all dressed up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to Wimbledon' sounds like a location for the houses, but it only means the final letter N. Wimbledon is a London suburb famous for its tennis tournament.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something made more beautiful by added ornament, as a hall adorned or decorated with flowers.

entries.clue: Cover music composed for two that takes in verse (5)

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside

blocks.note: a duet is music for two performers
V = verse

annotation.surface: A band records a cover version of a duet with an added verse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like a cover version of a song, which suits the music; it is a bed cover.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the quilt stuffed with down that goes over you in bed is a cover.

entries.clue: Drunk revises inebriation (7)

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A drunk goes over his work again while intoxicated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' wants to be the definition, matching 'inebriation'; it is the anagram indicator. Ivresse is the French word for drunkenness, also used in English.
annotation.definitionFit: Ivresse means drunkenness or intoxication.

entries.clue: “Indian singer” is false answer (5)

blocks.note: sham = false
A = answer

annotation.surface: A quiz-show answer, 'Indian singer', is ruled wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Indian singer' look like a quiz answer about a vocalist; the singer is a bird.
annotation.definitionFit: The shama is an Indian songbird of the thrush family.

entries.clue: This writer is past final stage in development (5)

blocks.note: this writer = I, so 'this writer is' = I'M
ago = in the past

annotation.surface: An author declares they are past their final stage of growth.
annotation.walkthrough: The imago is the adult insect, the last stage after larva and pupa.
annotation.definitionFit: The imago is the final, adult stage of an insect's metamorphosis.

entries.clue: Italian score’s recently added for air (9)

blocks.note: venti is Italian for twenty, a score
surface padding: says the next piece is joined on after the first
late = recently, as in 'of late'

annotation.surface: An Italian composer's score has just had a new tune added.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'air' look musical; a score is twenty and to air is to let fresh air in. The 's stands for 'has', joining the two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: letting fresh air through a stuffy room; both also mean bringing an opinion out for discussion.

entries.clue: First person given audition gets attention (3)

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is as heard

blocks.note: I is the first person pronoun

annotation.surface: The first actor to audition catches the director's attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Audition' looks like a tryout; here it means hearing.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiomatic sense: to catch someone's eye is to get their attention, and keeping an eye on things is watching them.

entries.clue: Born in Cambridge alongside Backs (3)

indicators.note: the backs of words are their last letters

blocks.note: last letters of iN, CambridgE, alongsidE

annotation.surface: Someone was born in Cambridge next to the Backs.
annotation.walkthrough: The Backs is the stretch of college lawns along the river in Cambridge, which makes 'Backs' look like a place name; it takes the back letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Née, 'born' in French, introduces a woman's maiden name.

entries.clue: Destroy pests initially missed in old art gallery (11)

indicators.note: the first letter is missing
the pests go inside the gallery

blocks.note: ex = former, old
the Tate, the London art gallery
vermin = pests; without its first letter, ERMIN goes inside TATE

annotation.surface: Pest control is called in to an old art gallery to wipe out the vermin.
annotation.walkthrough: EX plus T(ERMIN)ATE. The Tate is the national art gallery in London.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with the pest-control sense in play: wiping out every last one of something.
